items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
PDL-CUL-23-014, Regional Operating Support for Public Art Galleries
notes: Rod Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development & Legislative Services, introduced the report noting that it addresses eligibility for operating funding for public art galleries in the Region of Waterloo. He indicated that the report highlights a decision made by Council in June 2000 to establish public art galleries as an area municipal responsibility, which has prevented them from receiving operating funds from the Region for the past 23 years. In addition to the historical context, the report outlines the financial implications of this decision and presents two budget options for consideration.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
COR-CFN-23-036, Q3 2023 Plan and Financial Update
notes:
Connie MacDonald, Chief Communications and Strategy Officer, spoke to the Q3 2023 Plan and Financial Update report. She emphasized the collaborative efforts over the past four years, during which the Region has actively worked with community partners on the six strategic focus areas outlined in the 2019-2023 Strategic Plan. The report serves as a comprehensive final update to that strategic plan that saw several notable achievements. These include a significant reduction in Greenhouse Gas emissions, noteworthy advancements in Grand River Transit (GRT) ridership and service expansion, collaborative partnerships with Indigenous and BIPOC communities on health services, and the successful initiation of the Child Care Subsidy access pilot.

C. Dyer presented the financial outcomes from the Q3 2023 Plan and Financial Update report. He noted that for the first three quarters of 2023, the region anticipates a surplus of approximately 0.8% of the overall tax levy designated for Regional services. This represents a slight enhancement from the previous report based on mid-year results. The positive shift can be primarily attributed to a surge in revenue from public transit fares, stemming from increased ridership. Additionally, he highlighted the Region's capital program continues to progress, currently estimating about 68% of the overall budget. A comprehensive report based on year-end results is slated for release in the early part of 2024, providing a more detailed assessment of the Region's financial standing.

items.title: COR-ADM-23-003, Waterloo Region Police Service Operating Surplus
notes:
C. Dyer spoke to the Waterloo Region Police Service Operating Surplus report, underscoring its purpose to provide context for the motion put forth by Councillor C. Huinink. He highlighted the current practice, where any operating surplus within the police services operating budget is retained by the police. This surplus is then allocated on an as-required basis at year-end to police reserves, following the guidelines outlined in the police board policy. He noted that a comprehensive review of similar practices across the province was conducted by the staff. The findings revealed a range of approaches, with some jurisdictions opting to retain the surplus within the police service, while others see the surplus returning to the municipality. He explained that the different approaches may stem from the absence of specific legislative guidance on the treatment of police surpluses in both the Municipal Act and the Police Services Act. He further highlighted that, as of the end of 2022, the reserve balances for police services amounts to approximately $46 million.

In response to a question from the committee, C. Dyer clarified that the report focuses on the surplus specifically. Within the police services budget, there exists a provision for reserves, mainly allocated for capital reserves, vehicles, and buildings. These reserves are integral components of the Police Services Capital Program.

Received for information.

items.title: Councillor C. Huinink Notice of Motion
notes:
Councillor C. Huinink addressed her motion, suggesting a distribution wherein 50% of any future surpluses would be retained for Waterloo Regional Police Services (WRPS) reserve funds, while the remaining 50% would be returned to the Region. She emphasized that such a distribution could potentially alleviate financial pressures on WRPS.

During the Committee discussion, members shared comments on various aspects, including insights on the motion, considerations about surpluses, reflections on the relationship between WRPS and the Region, observations regarding neighbouring municipalities, and discussions on best practices.

In response to a Committee question, Graham Walsh, Regional Solicitor/Director, Legal Services, addressed the relationship between Waterloo Regional Police Services (WRPS) and the Region, clarifying that they operate in a co-governance structure. He emphasized that WRPS is subject to the Police Services Act, which is distinct from the governing framework of the Regional Municipality of Waterloo.

motions.item_title: Councillor C. Huinink Notice of Motion
motions.text: Whereas the Region is facing yet another difficult budget year; And Whereas housing, homelessness, drug addiction and mental health services continue to need additional resources; And Whereas all operating departments of the Region do not retain any surplus that has been able to be achieved; And Whereas the Waterloo Region Police Service in the recent years has been approved to transfer 100% of its surpluses to its own reserve funds; Therefore, Be It Resolved that any future surpluses be retained 50% to WRPS reserve funds and 50% returned to the Region.
motions.text_html:
Whereas the Region is facing yet another difficult budget year;

And Whereas housing, homelessness, drug addiction and mental health services continue to need additional resources;

And Whereas all operating departments of the Region do not retain any surplus that has been able to be achieved;

And Whereas the Waterloo Region Police Service in the recent years has been approved to transfer 100% of its surpluses to its own reserve funds;

Therefore, Be It Resolved that any future surpluses be retained 50% to WRPS reserve funds and 50% returned to the Region.
